paper_metadata.title: Financial Portfolio Optimization: a QUBO Formulation for Sharpe Ratio Maximization

summary: The paper formulates two QUBO encodings for Sharpe-ratio-based portfolio optimization on a 432-asset S&P500 dataset (2013–2020), with QUBO sizes of 3888 and 5184 binary variables, and calibrates penalty parameters using 20 runs per (λ0, λ1) pair before drawing 10 feasible solutions per configuration. Using D-Wave QBSolv and D-Wave Hybrid, the authors report Sharpe ratio distributions (via violin plots), feasibility rates, and asset-selection statistics, and find that the proposed quadratic reformulation with QBSolv is the best QUBO performer but does not surpass a classical PyPortfolioOpt baseline. The work’s main quantitative contribution is demonstrating that large dense QUBOs with discretization granularity around 0.002 and λ1 = 300 can be feasibly solved on current D-Wave-based tools, while still trailing classical portfolio optimizers in solution quality.

experiments.description: Sharpe Ratio Proxy QUBO formulation (discretized asset weights with K=9 per asset) solved with D-Wave QBSolv solver on S&P500 daily data (log-returns).

algorithm.variant: Sharpe Ratio Proxy QUBO (Venturelli & Kondratyev style coefficients)

hyperparameters.feasibility_constraint: sum_i sum_k dk * x_{i,k} = 1 (enforced via penalty H1)

problem_formulation.objective_function: Proxy QUBO: sum_i a_i * sum_k dk x_{i,k} + sum_{i<j} b_{ij} * (sum_k dk x_{i,k}) * (sum_k dk x_{j,k}) where a_i = mu_i / sigma_i and b_{ij} = rho_{ij}
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty term: H1 = ( sum_i sum_k dk x_{i,k} - 1 )^2 weighted by lambda_1
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Q = lambda_0 * H0 + lambda_1 * H1, H0 as objective (above), H1 as constraint penalty

problem_instance.description: Portfolio selection maximizing a proxy objective derived from asset-level Sharpe-like coefficients and pairwise correlations, discretized investment per asset.

dataset_specification.date_range: 2013-2020 (daily adjusted close prices from Yahoo! Finance)
preprocessing_steps: Remove null values and assets with consecutive nulls
Compute simple returns Rt and log-returns log(1+Rt)
Compute sample expected returns and sample covariance matrix, annualized using factor 252
Remove assets with negative expected return

quantum_resources.notes: Number of binary variables in the QUBO = 3888 (432 assets * 9 discretization bits). Paper does not report physical qubit embedding, embedding overhead, nor any gate-model circuit metrics.

hardware.notes: Authors state use of D-Wave's QBSolv solver. Paper does not specify whether QBSolv was run purely classically or submitted subproblems to a specific D-Wave QPU, nor which QPU generation was used.

noise_model.notes: No explicit noise modelling or noise parameters are reported.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Filter feasible solutions (sum weights = 1), collect 10 feasible solutions per fixed lambda pair and report Sharpe Ratio distribution

runs.calibration_grid_search: grid over lambda0 and lambda1, 20 runs per lambda-config to assess feasibility

implementation_details.feasibility_tolerance: for proxy: exact equality of discretized sum to 1 enforced via penalty (feasible solutions reported)
implementation_details.notes: Proxy encodes a_i = mu_i/sigma_i and b_ij = rho_ij; no change-of-variables y used here

convergence_data.notes: Authors collected 10 feasible solutions per fixed lambda configuration after calibration; calibration used 20 runs per lambda-pair to assess feasibility. Detailed per-run objective values/statistics not tabulated in numeric form in the paper.

results.value: sum_i sum_k d_k * x_{i,k} = 1 (enforced via penalty H1)
exact equality to 1 via penalty (proxy formulation)

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit empirical or asymptotic speedup claims reported for this experiment.

inferred_scaling.qubo_couplers: Up to O(M^2) pairwise quadratic terms in worst case (dense QUBO)
inferred_scaling.embedding_overhead: Not reported; physical qubit count could be substantially larger due to minor-embedding on D-Wave hardware

complexity_analysis.notes: The paper does not provide any formal algorithmic complexity or wall-clock comparisons. From the formulation one can infer that problem size scales linearly in assets times discretization bits and that the QUBO coupling matrix can be dense, implying O((N*K)^2) couplers.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; no asymptotic or empirical scaling comparison vs classical QUBO/portfolio solvers.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large-scale, high-quality QPU or hybrid solver capable of handling >5000 binary variables with better solution quality and/or time-to-solution than classical QUBO solvers and convex portfolio optimizers.

experiments.description: Proposed quadratic reformulation QUBO (discretized y variables with H=12 per asset, faithful quadratic reformulation of Max-Sharpe) solved with D-Wave QBSolv solver on S&P500 daily data (log-returns).

algorithm.variant: Proposed QUBO based on quadratic reformulation (minimize y^T Sigma y s.t. mu^T y = 1) discretized into binary variables

hyperparameters.ck_formula: ck = 2^(k-1)/10 for k=1..H-1; cH = 1/mu_min - sum_{k=1..H-1} ck
hyperparameters.feasibility_constraint: penalty on (mu^T y - 1)^2 weighted by lambda_1
hyperparameters.feasibility_tolerance: mu^T y within neighborhood of 1 up to factor 2.5e-4 (derived from min discretization * min expected return)

problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize y^T Sigma y, subject to mu^T y = 1; y variables discretized and embedded in QUBO with H0 representing y^T Sigma y and H1 representing (mu^T y - 1)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty term H1 = (mu^T y - 1)^2 weighted by lambda_1
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Q = lambda_0 * H0 + lambda_1 * H1, with H0 = discretized y^T Sigma y and H1 = discretized constraint penalty

problem_instance.description: Quadratic Max-Sharpe portfolio optimization via change-of-variables y (mu^T y = 1) discretized into binary variables; final portfolio recovered as w = y / (sum_i y_i).

dataset_specification.date_range: 2013-2020 (daily adjusted close prices from Yahoo! Finance)
preprocessing_steps: Remove null values and assets with consecutive nulls
Compute simple returns Rt and log-returns log(1+Rt)
Compute sample expected returns and sample covariance matrix, annualized using factor 252
Remove assets with negative expected return

quantum_resources.notes: Number of binary variables in the QUBO = 5184 (432 assets * 12 discretization bits). No physical qubit embedding or gate-model metrics reported.

hardware.notes: Authors state use of D-Wave's QBSolv solver for the proposed formulation. Specific QPU or QBSolv configuration not provided.

noise_model.notes: No explicit noise modelling or mitigation described.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Feasibility check: mu^T y within tolerance; retrieve 10 feasible solutions per fixed lambda pair and report Sharpe Ratio distribution; compute final w = y / sum(y)

runs.calibration_grid_search: grid over lambda0 and lambda1, 20 runs per lambda-config to assess feasibility

implementation_details.notes: Discretization range up to 1/mu_min used to bound y variables; H=12 yields step 0.1

convergence_data.notes: 10 feasible solutions per calibrated lambda pair were collected; calibration used 20 runs per lambda-pair. The paper reports that the best QUBO performer was the Proposed Formulation with QBSolv, but does not provide numeric convergence traces.

results.value: Proposed Formulation with QBSolv reported as best among QUBO solutions

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit speedup claims demonstrated; authors discuss solver-dependent performance differences but not speedups.

inferred_scaling.qubo_couplers: Up to O(M^2) couplers (dense quadratic objective term y^T Sigma y yields many pairwise interactions)
inferred_scaling.embedding_overhead: Not reported; minor-embedding on D-Wave hardware could inflate physical qubit count substantially

complexity_analysis.notes: The paper does not present formal complexity bounds or runtime estimates. From the QUBO construction, problem size and QUBO density imply quadratic growth in couplers with M.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; although the QUBO has 5184 binary variables, no scaling or runtime advantage vs classical PyPortfolioOpt or classical QUBO solvers is demonstrated.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault-tolerant or significantly larger, lower-noise QPUs able to solve dense 5000+ variable QUBOs faster and with higher-quality Sharpe ratios than classical convex and heuristic solvers.
